problems.title: Invalid normal-cone cancellation in equation (3.29)
problems.source_locator: Theorem 3.11, p.20, displayed subgradient formula and (3.29); generic function stratification Theorem 3.29, p.31
problems.hypotheses: Definable X and Y; X locally closed; Y C2 near base point; strong (a); x near base and unit v in limiting N_X(x).
problems.decisive_evidence: X=epi(u^2), Y={0}, x=(t,t^2), v=(2t,-1)/sqrt(1+4t^2), t>0. All hypotheses hold. Inner product is positive. The true squared distance to partial g is 1+t^2+t^4, while the claimed squared bound is t^2+t^4.
problems.counterevidence: The example satisfies the final (b=) conclusion. A signed h and the two-sided nonsmooth KL inequality give a replacement proof in the report appendix.
problems.core_dependency: Equation (3.29) supplies the small-subgradient bound needed by the claimed strong-(a) to (b=) implication; the generic epigraph use relies on this implication in the locally closed case.
problems.repair_status: Replacement signed-KL proof checked analytically, including signs, limiting normals, local closedness, uniformity and s phi'(s) ->0; author adoption unknown.
problems.impact_boundary: Invalid core proof step, not a false final Theorem 3.11; no whole-paper failure.

independent_verification.decisive_source_claim: Theorem 3.11, source p.20, equation (3.29), supplies the small-subgradient estimate for the stated strong-(a) to (b=) derivation; p.31 uses that implication after establishing strong (a) for locally closed epigraph strata.
independent_verification.hypotheses_checked: The convex closed semialgebraic epigraph w>=u^2 and singleton target satisfy definability, local closedness and C2 target hypotheses. Strong (a) is automatic because the singleton normal space is the ambient space. The specified unit vector is an actual outward limiting normal.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: At x=(t,t^2), v=(2t,-1)/sqrt(1+4t^2), t>0, <v,x>=t^2/sqrt(1+4t^2)>0. The positive branch gives partial g={((1+lambda)v,x):lambda>=0}; minimization gives squared distance 1+t^2+t^4, whereas the proposed squared bound is t^2+t^4. A cone cannot cancel v by an unavailable negative normal. The ratio diverges, so an unspecified uniform factor does not repair the step.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The same example satisfies (b=), with normalized normal pairing tending to zero. Independently checked the report signed replacement h=-<v,x-PY(x)>+indicator_clX: use the positive normal v to obtain dist(0,partial h)<=K dist(x,Y). The actual BDLS reference Theorem 14, pp.568-569 (PDF 13-14), applies to both signs for lower-semicontinuous definable functions; Remark 8, p.570 (PDF15), expressly permits limiting subgradients. Local closedness, a smaller closed definable neighborhood, positive uniform radius on bounded (x,v), symmetry/range of DPY, and s phi-prime(s)->0 justify the claimed repair and passage from projected to full (b=) using the unaffected second part of Theorem 3.9.
independent_verification.severity_reason: A false central derivation, with traced generic-function dependency, supports proof-specific Major. Theorem 3.11 is not declared false, and the replacement proof is verified without claiming author adoption.
independent_verification.later_author_text: Read retained dissertation PDF43-44, printed30-31; it repeats the same g and cancellation. This is version-specific counterevidence, not proof of journal wording.

problems.title: C1 target manifold does not imply Lipschitz normal variation
problems.hypotheses: Arbitrary X,Y, base in Y, C1 retraction with local distance control, Y a C1 embedded manifold.
problems.decisive_evidence: X=Y=graph |t|^(3/2); vertical C1 retraction satisfies the distance condition. Projected gap is zero but full gap/distance equals 3/[2 sqrt(t) sqrt(1+9t/4) sqrt(1+t)] -> infinity.
problems.counterevidence: Later applications in Propositions 3.10 and 3.21 and Theorems 3.11/3.25 already require C2 or higher target smoothness.
problems.core_dependency: False estimate (3.22) is the direct step passing projected strong (a) to arbitrary target points.
problems.repair_status: C2 target suffices by locally Lipschitz normal projectors and the source triangle argument; checked.
problems.impact_boundary: The C1 statement is false. No demonstrated failure of the higher-smoothness downstream applications.

independent_verification.decisive_source_claim: Theorem 3.9(1), source p.17, permits C1 target and C1 retraction; p.18 equation (3.22) assumes Lipschitz variation of its normal spaces.
independent_verification.hypotheses_checked: For X=Y=graph |u|^(3/2), the vertical projection is C1 and maps into the graph. Its distance bound follows from the locally bounded graph slope and Cauchy-Schwarz, including the localization of nearest graph points.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: The projected normal gap is zero. At (t,t^(3/2)) against the origin, the full gap divided by distance is 3/[2 sqrt(t) sqrt(1+9t/4) sqrt(1+t)], diverging as t decreases to zero. C1 gives continuous normal variation, not the linear estimate used in (3.22).
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: A C2 target has a C1 normal projector with locally bounded derivative, which supplies the missing Lipschitz estimate. Checked higher-smoothness premises in Proposition3.10, Theorem3.11, Proposition3.21 and Theorem3.25. Read dissertation PDF39-40, printed26-27, which repeats the C1 statement and estimate.
independent_verification.severity_reason: Minor is supported by the false low-smoothness theorem range and the fact that the cited downstream uses already satisfy the stronger smoothness. No failure of those applications is established.

problems.title: Strong (a) does not provide the stated actual-subgradient selection
problems.source_locator: Theorem 3.25, pp.29-30, first paragraph of p.30
problems.hypotheses: Symmetric locally Lipschitz f; symmetric C2 manifold M; f restricted to M C2; strong (a) along M; F=f composed with eigenvalues.
problems.decisive_evidence: Dimension one, f(t)=|t|^(3/2), M={0}. All symmetry, smoothness, and strong-(a) premises hold. F=f, Y=0, Z=3 sqrt(t)/2, partial F(0)={0}. The selection ratio is 3/(2 sqrt(t)) -> infinity.
problems.counterevidence: The final spectral theorem holds in this singleton example; graph-restriction normals are larger than actual epigraph subgradient selections.
problems.core_dependency: The false selection is the explicit justification of projected strong (a) used to claim the spectral transfer in Theorem 3.25.
problems.repair_status: A normal-space/tangential replacement is identified as needed; full general replacement not certified.
problems.impact_boundary: Proof-specific Major; no false final spectral theorem or algorithmic consequence established.

independent_verification.hypotheses_checked: One-by-one symmetric matrices are included. f(t)=|t|^(3/2) is locally Lipschitz and symmetric in dimension one; M={0} is symmetric C-infinity and f restricted to M is smooth. The restriction graph is a singleton, so epigraph strong (a) holds.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: For t>0, F=f, Y=0, Z=(3/2)sqrt(t), and partial F(0)={0}. Every actual subgradient selection therefore has ratio 3/(2 sqrt(t)), unbounded. The graph restriction normal space allows vectors that are not actual subgradients; the set-normal argument on source p.26 does not imply the stated membership.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The final spectral statement holds in this singleton example. A replacement through restriction-graph normals/tangential components would be needed; the report correctly does not certify a full general replacement or a false final spectral theorem. independent_verification.severity_reason: The false estimate is the explicit core proof of the strong-(a) spectral transfer, supporting a bounded proof-specific Major without claiming whole-paper or algorithmic failure.

problems.title: Uniform marginal noise does not imply conditional excitation
problems.source_locator: Assumption F and Theorem 6.2 p.42; independence and conditional lower bound p.58; A p.33 and E p.38
problems.hypotheses: All A1-A3 for every alpha and nu near every saddle; measurable G; gamma in (1/2,1); martingale-difference conditional fourth moments; domain condition; C4 M; negative manifold-Hessian eigenvalue; uniform marginals.
problems.decisive_evidence: C-infinity f(x)=-(||x||^2-1)^2, M=R2, S=unit circle. A Borel map with a tangential normalization correction of norm <=alpha||nu||^2/2 satisfies A. Start deterministically at zero, use a first uniform-disk noise to reach a uniform circle point, then choose nu_k=epsilon_k R_k J x_k. Each marginal is uniform on the disk, conditional mean zero and fourth moment 1/3, but the angle martingale has square-summable increments and converges almost surely on S. Radial Hessian eigenvalue -8.
problems.counterevidence: The source proof expressly intends noise independent of history. Conditional uniformity supplies the needed positive directional expectation and excludes the construction.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem 6.2 invokes Theorem 6.1(2c); unconditional marginals do not establish its conditional lower bound.
problems.repair_status: Conditional law given F_k uniform on a fixed-radius ball repairs the identified noise implication; separate regularity/localization matters remain.
problems.impact_boundary: Counterexample to the printed general-map theorem under marginal-only reading. Not a counterexample to intended fresh-noise subgradient/projected/proximal algorithms.

independent_verification.decisive_source_claim: AssumptionF and Theorem6.2 on source p.42 state uniform marginals; AssumptionE on p.38 gives martingale differences and conditional fourth moments. The proof on p.58 invokes independence and a uniform conditional directional expectation.
independent_verification.hypotheses_checked: For f(x)=-(||x||^2-1)^2, M=R2 and S the unit circle, every saddle has radial Hessian eigenvalue -8. The Borel generalized map in the report satisfies A1-A3 for every alpha>0 and every noise vector near each saddle; the exceptional origin is outside those local neighborhoods. All iterates remain in dom f, gamma=3/4 is allowed, and q=2 bounds the conditional fourth moment 1/3.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: On the tangential branch s=sqrt(1+alpha^2||nu||^2), the exact error is ||G_alpha(x,nu)-nu||=(s-1)/alpha<=alpha||nu||^2/2 and ||G||<=||nu||, so A1/A2 hold; A3 is vacuous for M=R2. Starting with independent uniform-disk nu0 at deterministic x0=0 gives uniform x1 on S. Subsequent nu_k=epsilon_k R_k Jx_k have conditionally zero mean and radial density 2r; rotational equivariance preserves uniform angle, so every unconditional marginal is uniform on the disk. The independent centered angular increments -arctan(alpha_k epsilon_k R_k) have summable variances <=alpha_k^2/2, hence the angle converges almost surely and the limiting iterate belongs to S with probability one.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_scope: Programmatic global search for independence/iid/fresh wording in all retained source pages identified the operative independence use on p.58, not an additional standing conditional-law premise. This search was indexing, not full scientific reading. The source proof plainly intends fresh noise. Conditional uniformity excludes the construction and gives E[|<nu,w>| | F_k]=r c_d; continuity of tangent projection then supplies the required positive lower bound.
independent_verification.severity_reason: Major only for the printed general-map theorem under marginal-only interpretation. No counterexample to the intended independently perturbed subgradient, projected or proximal algorithms is claimed; the report expressly records this interpretation boundary.

problems.title: C4 manifold does not make a C2 restriction C3
problems.source_locator: Theorem 6.2 application to C2-field Theorem 6.1, p.57; (A2) p.33
problems.hypotheses: C4 manifold and f restricted to it only C2; A/E, even fresh independent uniform noise, negative Hessian direction.
problems.decisive_evidence: M=R, f(t)=-t^2+|t|^(5/2), G=f'+nu. All A conditions hold; f''(0)=-2. F=-f' has F''(t)=-15/(8 sqrt(t)) for t>0 and is not C2.
problems.counterevidence: The C4 active-saddle definition in the actual corollaries includes C4 smoothness of the restricted function, so those applications meet the stronger premise.
problems.core_dependency: The proof claims F_p is C2 to invoke Theorem 6.1; geometric smoothness of M alone does not supply it.
problems.repair_status: Requiring f|M C3 makes f composed with P_M C3 for C4 M, so its negative gradient is C2.
problems.impact_boundary: Failure of a claimed regularity implication, not a proved failure of saddle avoidance.

independent_verification.decisive_source_claim: Source p.57 claims f composed with P_M is C3 because M is C4, in order to apply the C2-field Theorem6.1. A2 on p.33 assumes only C2 smoothness of the restriction.
independent_verification.hypotheses_checked: For M=R and f(t)=-t^2+|t|^(5/2), f is closed and C2, f-prime(0)=0 and f-double-prime(0)=-2. The exact gradient-plus-noise map satisfies all A conditions, and fresh independent bounded uniform noise satisfies E/F.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: For t>0 the negative-gradient field is 2t-(5/2)t^(3/2), whose second derivative is -15/(8 sqrt(t)); it is not C2 at the saddle.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Requiring f restricted to M to be C3 is sufficient because a C4 embedded manifold has C3 local projection. Definition2.1 on p.9 includes restriction smoothness in an active C4 manifold, so Corollaries6.3-6.4 already satisfy the stronger premise.
independent_verification.severity_reason: Minor regularity implication gap in the abstract application, not a proved stochastic nonconvergence failure.

problems.title: Auxiliary-process localization is not stable under shrinking the outer ball
problems.source_locator: Theorem 6.1(1) p.41; first proof paragraph p.50; Proposition 5.2 pp.39-40
problems.hypotheses: C2 field with unstable symmetric derivative at p; auxiliary process stays in B_(epsilon_p/2) for one fixed outer radius epsilon_p; deterministic summable-square/nonsummable steps; conditional centered excitation and bounded fourth moments; zero errors permitted; all stopping radii and starting indices.
problems.decisive_evidence: d=1, S={0}, X_k=0, epsilon=4, F(y)=y-y^2, alpha_k=(1/4)k^(-3/4), Y_1=1, independent xi_k=+-1/8, E=0. The maps preserve [1/2,3/2] strictly inside B_(epsilon/2)=B2, derivative >=1/2, inward endpoint increments alpha/8 and -5alpha/8. All displayed conditions hold for every stopping radius, but P(lim X in S)=1.
problems.counterevidence: The proof intends to choose an arbitrarily small Lyapunov neighborhood. The actual shadow process satisfies Y in B_(4delta), which permits this localization.
problems.core_dependency: The proof shrinks epsilon and assumes the process hypothesis remains available; existence in one original ball does not imply that.
problems.repair_status: Require local-process hypotheses at every sufficiently small outer radius, or a fixed-C shrinking bound Y in B_(C delta). This removes the demonstrated obstruction; not a full new proof certificate.
problems.impact_boundary: Standalone abstract theorem false as displayed; the actual shadow application's localization is stronger and is not refuted.

Corrected epsilon0 to4, the displayed containment to B_(epsilon0/2)=B2, and the stopping-radius range to delta<4. The original report/PDF and affected records were preserved before editing.

X_k=0 gives infinite stopping time for every positive delta<4 and every starting index. The next independent sign of magnitude1/8 is centered for the stated X/Y-history filtration, with fourth moment1/4096 and absolute excitation1/8 in both unit unstable directions. Errors are zero. Steps (1/4)k^(-3/4) are square summable and not summable.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: Both update maps have derivative at least1/2 on the interval for alpha<=1/4. Their inward extreme increments are alpha/8 at1/2 and -5alpha/8 at3/2, proving invariance for every sign sequence. Thus all displayed hypotheses hold for the corrected radius, but P(lim X in {0})=1. The retained symbolic interval calculation contains no epsilon choice and remains valid without rerun.

Proposition5.2 on pp.39-40 and equation8.8 on p.57 actually give Y in B_(4delta), so the shadow application has the stronger localization and is not refuted. Requiring the process hypotheses for every sufficiently small outer radius, or a fixed-C B_(Cdelta) localization, removes this obstruction; it is not claimed to certify the entire abstract theorem.
